articles.headline: Cavaliers promoting Brandon Weems to GM, sources say
articles.description: The Cavaliers are promoting Brandon Weems, who has been with the team for the past decade, to serve as general manager, sources told ESPN
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers are promoting Brandon Weems to serve as general manager under team president Koby Altman, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday.

Weems has been in the Cavaliers organization for the past decade, rising from scouting and personnel positions to be the team's assistant general manager since 2022. He replaces Mike Gansey, will was hired as the Philadelphia 76ers' president of basketball operations in May.

The 40-year-old Weems is a childhood friend and former high school teammate of LeBron James. James' agent, Rich Paul, referred to Weems as "basically LeBron's brother" during the superstar's free agency process this summer. Paul indicated that Weems' presence was a pro in the Cavaliers' pursuit before James ultimately chose to sign with the 76ers.

Prior to joining the Cavaliers, Weems was an assistant coach at Oakland University. He has also served on the staffs at Drexel and Kentucky, where he worked under coach John Calipari.

He played college basketball at Walsh University, winning an NAIA title in 2005.

articles.headline: Lamine Yamal reveals he has experienced racism 'a thousand times'
articles.description: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has revealed that he has experienced racism "a thousand times."
articles.body:
Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has revealed that he has experienced racism "a thousand times."

The 19-year-old said people can sometimes be "indirectly racist" and "without realising it," whilst stressing that "what is wrong can never be accepted."

The World Cup winner, who has started this season in fine form for Barcelona, scoring seven goals in six La Liga matches, spoke in an interview with Movistar, which will be broadcast on Sept. 18 in Spain about the subject of racism.

In extracts shown on social media, Yamal said: "A thousand times [I've experienced racism].

"People are indirectly racist towards you, even though they don't realise it. There are lots of comments or looks that are racist, and they don't realise it."

Yamal has quickly become one of the most iconic faces in football after rising to prominence during the 2024 Euros, which Spain also won.

And he explains now that while he does not accept racism, he is no longer phased by it.

"I'm at a place where, it's not that it's accepted, because you can never accept something that's wrong, but it doesn't bother you [when it happens]," he added.

Yamal spoke further on a specific example of being unfazed by the comments, describing a time when he did not react despite being called Black by an opposition fan.

- Harry Kane on Ballon d'Or: 73 goals last season 'speaks for itself'

- Man City's Enzo Maresca: 'If I don't win it's a disaster'

- Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta on Fabian Hürzeler falling out: 'That's all in the past'

People ended up surprised by Yamal's lack of reaction but he explained why he did not react.

"There's that well-known video from the Bernabéu where people were shouting all sorts of things at Raphinha and me, and everyone was surprised by my reaction," he said.

"Being called 'Black' doesn't bother me in the slightest -- I am Black, after all.

"It's another matter entirely that it's wrong, because he's saying it to offend me, but if I'm playing a match and he's paid for a ticket to watch me, I'm not going to get angry just because I've been disrespected."

articles.headline: Rio Ngumoha 'deserves' England call - Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola
articles.description: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has praised the attitude of forward Rio Ngumoha and said he "absolutely deserves" his call up to the England national team.
articles.body:
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has praised the attitude of forward Rio Ngumoha and said he "absolutely deserves" his call up to the England national team.

Ngumoha earned his first senior cap for England in a friendly against New Zealand back in June, having been included in Thomas Tuchel's pre-World Cup training camp.

The 18-year-old is one of a number of players who will be hoping to make an impression on the England boss in the upcoming international break, as well as midfielder Alex Scott who worked under Iraola at AFC Bournemouth.

"Very happy for both," Iraola said. "I think they both absolutely deserve it. They both also went to help the national team before the tournament and I am sure they both did a good job. I can only speak so well about both. It's very deserved, they are very ready and I hope they both enjoy it."

Ngumoha has already made five appearances for Liverpool this season and started in Tuesday's 3-1 victory over Tottenham Hotspur in the Carabao Cup. While the forward has traditionally played on the left, Iraola prefers his wingers to play on both flanks and has praised the way Ngumoha has embraced the challenge.

"The other day, for example, against Spurs he probably didn't have his best start to the game but I like how he came back from that," the Liverpool boss said. "He lost a couple of duels at the beginning. [Destiny] Udogie is a very strong player. But after, he did his job. In the first two goals, he appears. Everything comes from the situations he goes one v one and he takes good decisions.

"The play finishes on the other side but he is part of that build up for the goal and that is what we are trying to put into him. He has to still adapt to the rhythm of the league because he is still very young, he has just turned 18. But has the quality to be involved in those kind of plays and I'm liking especially his attitude, because he's not like: 'I prefer to play here.' He's ready to do what we need. I'm very happy also because they've called him for the national team."

- England Nations League squad: Trent Alexander-Arnold, Cole Palmer recalled after World Cup snub

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: A+ to F

- Trent Alexander-Arnold, Cole Palmer challenged to 'perform' for England by Thomas Tuchel

This weekend will see Iraola return to the Vitality Stadium to face former club Bournemouth, where he will be hoping to oversee his second Premier League victory of the season.

Asked how he feels about facing his old team, Iraola said: "I think in the personal side I'm really looking forward to meeting and hugging them, players that I love, staff that I have worked with that I appreciate so much. I was pushing for them yesterday when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best.

"But there is another part that is the most important one right now. That we need to go there and win and beat them and be as ruthless as possible. And leave all the talking for after the game."

articles.headline: Michael Carrick: 'Ridiculous to think' I'm under pressure at Man United
articles.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has said it's "ridiculous" to think that he could be under pressure so early in the season.
articles.body:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has said it's "ridiculous" to think that he could be under pressure so early in the season.

Carrick won the permanent job at Old Trafford after winning 12 of his 17 games as interim boss last season.

The new campaign has started slowly with just two wins from six games in all competitions and back-to-back home defeats to Manchester City and Brighton.

But speaking at a news conference on Friday, Carrick rejected a suggestion his position could already be under threat.

"I think that'll be a lot longer than one or two games of results," he said.

"In terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, I'm not thinking 'how long have I got?'

"It's ridiculous to think that way in a position that I'm in. That's just not on the radar. It's two or three games that we haven't had certain results, and two or three games too many because I really hate losing.

"But that doesn't mean that the world caves in."

Carrick came out fighting at his news conference following a difficult week for the club and bit back at another suggestion that fans want to see him show more emotion in interviews and on the touchline after negative results.

"I need to show more emotion?" Carrick replied.

"In what way? In what way? I'm asking, how? What do you want me to show?

"We don't like losing football matches, so it's not that I don't feel the emotion of losing football matches, but it doesn't affect how I think about what we need to do next."

Following the controversial derby defeat to Manchester City, United suffered another setback on Wednesday by giving up a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 to Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

Afterwards, Carrick made clear that the result was his responsibility.

He has consistently refused the chance to make public excuses for poor results and on Friday insisted that he will continue to shoulder any blame himself.

"That's why I'm here," he said.

- Why Man United's wantaway 15-year-old wonderkid, JJ Gabriel, is so highly rated

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: A+ to F

- Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years

"It's my responsibility. I'm fine with that. It's not a blame game. We all search for things to look at and point at and find blame, and sometimes it gets almost like too much of a thing of wanting to find someone to blame or something to blame. Blame me, no problem.

"I'll take the responsibility. It's not about blaming people.

"It's about finding solutions and being better, and that's as a whole football club, you know, as a group of players, as staff, as owners, supporters, it's a whole collective thing.

"I'm totally happy taking responsibility, absolutely no problem with that, it doesn't bother me. I just know where we want to get to and we want to get there fast."

articles.headline: Dejan Kulusevski will be 'like a new signing' for Tottenham - Roberto De Zerbi
articles.description: The eagerly-anticipated return of playmaker Dejan Kulusevski will be like a "new signing" for Tottenham, according to head coach Roberto De Zerbi.
articles.body:
The eagerly-anticipated return of playmaker Dejan Kulusevski will be like a "new signing" for Tottenham, according to head coach Roberto De Zerbi.

Kulusevski has not played for Spurs since the end of the 2024-25 campaign due to a right patella injury, which has essentially put the career of the Sweden international on hold for 19 months and ruled him out of the summer World Cup.

There finally appears to be light at the end of the tunnel after Kulusevski returned to full training this week.

He first returned in August only to suffer a small setback, but the 26-year-old is back and whilst he is not ready to face Aston Villa on Saturday, a first comeback appearance could be on the horizon in October or November.

"We have to manage Deki in the best way we can, with the medical staff, physical staff, but it's a great thing for us," De Zerbi said. "He's a good player, he's a good guy and he deserves to play again.

"We have to work day by day, also for Deki it's important the international break because when he will be at the top of condition and pass over the injury, I think it's a great signing. A new signing for us, another new signing."

Kulusevski was arguably Spurs' best player during an injury-affected 2024-25 campaign before he missed the whole of last season due to this long-standing knee problem.

It was a similar story for James Maddison, who sustained anterior cruciate ligament damage last August before he returned ahead of schedule in May to help Tottenham stay in the Premier League.

Maddison's pre-season this time around has been hampered before a shoulder issue at Brentford on the opening day provided a further setback, but after an encouraging cameo in a 3-1 loss at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, the 29-year-old is primed for more minutes against Villa.

De Zerbi added: "Listen, James is working with the team in the last 10, 15 days. Maybe less than 15 days and even if he's a technical player, he needs to be fit, to stay in a good condition.

- Are Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham bad, or just unlucky? Against Aston Villa, we'll find out

- Omar Marmoush certain Tottenham close to finding the key to unlock their attack

"When he arrives to the best condition, it's very important for us as a personality, as a characteristic, as a quality, as an experience. The quality of his passes are different than the others."

Pedro Porro and Sandro Tonali sat out Tuesday's defeat to Liverpool but are available for Saturday's lunchtime kick-off.

Spurs are winless and goalless in the Premier League after four matches. However, Villa are below them in the table in 19th with only one point.

De Zerbi said: "You have to stay calm, to be confident in what you are doing, what the players are doing. They have my full confidence."

articles.headline: Fantasy Baseball Forecaster Playoff Round 2, Week 2: Sept. 21-27
articles.description: Set your lineups for fantasy baseball's final week with our preview featuring pitcher rankings, hitter ratings and schedule observations.
articles.body:
This is it! The final week of the 2026 fantasy baseball season has arrived. If you've made it this far, congratulations! The final seven days should be a wild race to the finish line, both in the real game and in our own leagues.

Week 25 is one of the more balanced weeks on the schedule, with one exception: The Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees begin their week-opening series with a Tuesday doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. One of those games makes up their May 23 postponement. The extra game gives both teams a seven-game final week.

All of the other 28 teams play exactly six games -- and 14 of those 28 split those six games evenly between home and the road. This is a "quality over quantity" week when it comes to matchups analysis. Additionally, most teams begin their weeks on Tuesday, as there are only three games scheduled for Monday.

Remember that MLB schedules all games on its final day, Sunday, Sept. 27, to start within a 15 minute window of one another (between 3:05 p.m. and 3:20 p.m. ET). This is by design to try and heighten the drama of real-life playoff races, but it also creates many mad, 3-4 hour dashes to the finish line in fantasy baseball leagues.

Get your popcorn -- I mean, your peanuts and Cracker Jack -- ready!

articles.headline: Man City's Enzo Maresca: 'If I don't win it's a disaster'
articles.description: Enzo Maresca is refusing to get carried away with Manchester City's flying start to the season, acknowledging pressure could quickly mount if results turn.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca is refusing to get carried away with Manchester City's flying start to the season, acknowledging pressure could quickly mount if results turn.

City continued their fine run of form by brushing aside Championship Norwich 5-0 to reach the Carabao Cup fourth round on Thursday.

Since losing to Arsenal in the Community Shield, City have won their last six matches in all competitions -- a fine start by Maresca after stepping into the void left by Pep Guardiola.

The City manager, whose side next face Sunderland on Sunday, said: "I'm really happy. I said in the first press conference, for me to be in this club is a privilege and to be in this club after a legend like Pep is a privilege.

"I know if I don't win it's a disaster, and it's normal, but I don't spend my day thinking who was here before and for how many years.

"I'm just here to focus on what we can do better, improve the team and trying to win games.

"I'm very happy with these five or six games in a row but now the main focus is just on the next one and I'm not thinking that we won six in a row because those games are finished. We focus on the next one and then we have the international break."

City made 10 changes for the visit of the Canaries, who fielded a weakened side themselves.

Teenager Floyd Samba stole the show on his senior debut, scoring twice as he took the place of the rested Erling Haaland at centre-forward.

Samba also had a hand in a goal for Rayan Cherki while winger Allan Elias, signed from Palmeiras for £34 million last month, also scored on his first appearance for the club.

A strong night for the City academy was capped when 18-year-old Ryan McAidoo came off the bench to add the fifth in the last minute.

In all there were seven City academy graduates on the field. Nico O'Reilly, Rico Lewis and Kaden Braithwaite also featured for the hosts, while Dan Grimshaw and Jacob Wright were in the Norwich side.

Maresca said: "We have different competitions. We have many games and we are just at the beginning of the season.

"The ones that played are going to play Premier League or Champions League games because the season is long.

"It was very important we gave rest to the ones that played back-to-back 90 minutes against Porto and [Manchester] United. Hopefully they can be full of energy for Sunday's game that will be a strong game."

articles.headline: Kylian Mbappé: I want to bring Ballon d'Or to Bernabéu despite boos
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé has reiterated his desire to win the Ballon d'Or but has called for more support from Real Madrid fans after a trophyless two years at the club.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé has reiterated his desire to win the Ballon d'Or but has called for more support from Real Madrid fans after a trophyless two years at the club.

The 27-year-old -- who is now the top scorer in World Cup history after adding 10 goals to his tally this summer -- is among the favourites for the award alongside the likes of Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal.

That is despite the fact that Madrid were beaten to the LaLiga title by Yamal's Barcelona and knocked out of the Champions League at the quarterfinal stage by Kane's Bayern Munich.

Madrid are currently second in LaLiga having slipped up against Real Betis, a match in which Mbappé missed a penalty.

"I think it can be a good year, but it doesn't depend on me," Mbappé said in an interview with AS.

"I want the Ballon d'Or to return to Real Madrid -- it's the best club in the world. I want it to return to the Bernabéu, to the Madrid fans.

"My objective is always to help my teammate, to do my best and to convince the people who vote, because at the end of the day, like you, they vote, right?"

The Frenchman also addressed the boos which have been directed at him and Vinícius Júnior by home fans at the Bernabéu.

"We didn't win anything last season, people are tired of it now," he said.

"I understand it. It's just that, like everything, there's a context to it. Sometimes when we win they [the Madrid fans] see that it's a difficult game.

"They need to know that right now we need the Bernabéu because it's the best stadium in the world, we have the best fans in the world and when we have them with us we're much stronger.

"But I also understand that there's an expectation. There's a part of it that I don't understand, which is normal, but they also have to understand that if we want to win titles, we're not going to win them without them."

articles.headline: New York Knicks offseason recap, early 2026-27 season preview
articles.description: The Knicks snapped their 53-year title drought in 2026. What's next for the historic franchise during the 2026-27 season?
articles.body:
It had been a long 53-year drought for the New York Knicks before last season's team finally broke through and brought a title back to New York City.

The Knicks now look primed for another deep run in the playoffs after retaining all five starters from their championship squad. They did lose Mitchell Robinson to the rival Boston Celtics in free agency but added Andre Drummond to fill in the backup center role behind Karl-Anthony Towns while also keeping Jordan Clarkson, Jose Alvarado, Landry Shamet and Mohamed Diawara for depth.

The Eastern Conference has become a powerhouse, but the Knicks are a big reason the power has shifted to the East. Can they become the first repeat NBA champion in eight seasons?

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the 2026-27 season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Friday. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for all 30 teams.

Quick links:

Roster | Depth chart | Transactions

More Knicks coverage | More NBA

Offseason at a glance

Key additions: Andre Drummond

Key retentions: Jordan Clarkson, Jose Alvarado, Landry Shamet, Mohamed Diawara

Key subtractions: Mitchell Robinson

The only question that followed the Knicks into the offseason after their dominant run to and through the NBA Finals was could this group be kept together? All the starters were locked in, but the bench unit was not, and owner James Dolan repeatedly stated he would not go into the punitive second apron. The Knicks couldn't keep valuable backup big Robinson around when Boston came with a lucrative offer (over $15 million per season), but key contributors Clarkson, Alvarado and Shamet all signed below-market deals to stay in New York and go for a repeat -- Vincent Goodwill

Zach Kram's offseason grade: B-

The Knicks' championship-winning roster remains mostly intact, and they signed Shamet and Alvarado to two of the best value contracts of the summer.

But second-apron concerns meant the champs' backup center spot declined from Robinson (with Ariel Hukporti at third string) to Andre Drummond. That downgrade could cost the Knicks a playoff game or two next spring. -- Kram

What we learned over the past few months

From Ben Golliver's offseason lessons piece: The second apron is more powerful than ever.

On paper, the Knicks are the ideal candidates to spend past the NBA's second apron. After all, the franchise was valued at nearly $10 billion in the latest Forbes rankings, and that was before it won its first championship since 1973.

With Madison Square Garden setting records for ticket prices and the Knicks spending months as the toast of the NBA's largest market, surely ownership would be willing to spend whatever it takes to keep the band together. Right?

articles.body:
After an eventful July full of big trades, intriguing signings and the game's biggest star shocking everyone by heading East, the NBA offseason is nearly complete. And with the regular-season schedule now out, it's time to start thinking about the 2026-27 season.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for every team.

Check out the rollout schedule below, with stories added daily:

Quick links:

Free agency buzz | FA grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Schedule | More NBA coverage

Atlantic Division

Philadelphia 76ers: Sept. 14

Key additions: F LeBron James, G Jaylen Brown, G Anfernee Simons, F Dean Wade, G Labaron Philon Jr., G Kentavious Caldwell-Pope

Key subtractions: F Paul George, C Andre Drummond, G Quentin Grimes, G Kelly Oubre Jr.

No team changed its fortunes from April to July as drastically as the 76ers. Taking advantage of Boston's desire to get out of the Jaylen Brown business enabled it to accomplish so much: getting a motivated All-Star feeling the sting of rejection following a career year, dumping George's contract and putting themselves in position to be attractive to an all-time great in James, who was looking for a new challenge. They also lessened their dependency on Joel Embiid's bothersome health as he will turn 33 during the season.

They filled in the blanks by adding Caldwell-Pope and Wade as plug-and-play wings, changing the complexion of their franchise in several swoops. If nothing else, they won the offseason. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full 76ers offseason recap/season preview

Boston Celtics: Sept. 15

Key additions: Paul George, Mitchell Robinson, Mike Conley

Key subtractions: Jaylen Brown, Nikola Vucevic

Key retentions: Neemias Queta, Jordan Walsh, Ron Harper Jr.

Boston responded to its first early playoff exit since 2021 by boldly trading Brown to the 76ers, ending his fruitful partnership with Jayson Tatum. The move should improve the Celtics' long-term flexibility to build around Tatum, but next year's iteration will require the aging George to discover the fountain of youth. The 36-year-old forward has played in 60 games just once in the past seven seasons.

Even so, this shouldn't be viewed as a gap year. The Celtics return a cohesive nucleus, and they added Robinson's defense and rebounding to shore up a frontcourt rotation that was overwhelmed in the postseason.

If Tatum returns to superstar form in his first fully healthy season since a May 2025 Achilles injury, the Celtics will have a chance to win at least 50 games for the sixth straight year. Securing Banner 19, however, will likely require finding a superstar replacement for Brown sometime down the road. -- Ben Golliver

articles.headline: Witnessing Jacob Misiorowski's Cy Young-worthy season
articles.description: What's it like seeing a Cy Young favorite unleash a 105 mph fastball? We asked those around the Brewers' breakout star.
articles.body:
Jacob Misiorowski will have to wait until November to see if his first full major league season ends with a National League Cy Young Award, but the Milwaukee Brewers ace is the runaway winner when it comes to oohs and aahs drawn on the mound.

The 24-year-old has thrown 1,053 fastballs over 100 mph this season -- 582 more than anyone else in the sport. Powered by that unparalleled heat, "The Miz" leads the majors with a 1.89 ERA, 0.81 WHIP and 243 strikeouts.

What is it like watching MLB's next great flamethrower dominate the sport? Ahead of his final scheduled start of the 2026 regular season, we asked Misiorowski's teammates what stood out most about his breakout year.

'The velocity jumps out for sure'

Misiorowski joined Jordan Hicks, Aroldis Chapman and Mason Miller as the only four pitchers since pitch tracking began in 2008 to throw 500 or more pitches at 100-plus mph in a single season. But even those three fellow flamethrowers pale in comparison to Miz's total number of triple-digit pitches. Hicks is second on the list with 659 pitches at 100 mph in 2018, but he, Chapman and Miller were able to air it out in short relief stints while Miziorowski has done it in a starting role.

Infielder David Hamilton: "A starter throwing that hard for that long is incredible. I sneak a peek at the board. The velocity jumps out for sure."

Catcher William Contreras: "For some people, watching him pitch that fast is out of this world. Now that I've gone the whole year catching Miz, it's gotten normal for me."

Reliever Chad Patrick: "I got to see him pitch in 2024. He was bringing it then. You start to question when he's throwing 99. Is something wrong? But nothing is wrong. He's doing his thing."

Starter Brandon Woodruff: "I would reference [Jacob] deGrom because he's the closest thing to what he's doing. He's throwing fastballs to one spot, and you see how successful he is. You can do that. Just get it over the plate and you can expand from there."

Outfielder Jackson Chourio: "I start a game thinking I have to be active out there -- but no, you don't."

Outfielder Christian Yelich: "Often they know it's coming. Sometimes they get to it. Most of the time they don't."

'Like a flash'

One pitch stands out from the rest of Miz's blazing heaters this season: A 105.5 mph laser to Chicago Cubs NL MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong on June 26. It's the fastest pitch thrown this year in MLB -- and the fastest ever by a starting pitcher. 

Contreras: "That pitch was like a flash. I'm thankful for him being on my team and not another."

Outfielder Garrett Mitchell: "It was electric. Every time he throws, we're expecting something great like that. I looked up [at another pitch] and saw 104. I was like, 'Man, this guy is throwing fuel up there.'"

Woodruff: "It's hard to hit 95, so 105 is really hard. I remember when I was hitting. No thank you."

Hamilton: "I don't know how [Crow-Armstrong] fouled that pitch off. That's the most impressive thing about it."

articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Sept. 17: Bey signs extension with Pelicans

Saddiq Bey terms: Three years, $55.5 million

Grade: B

Bey arrived in New Orleans as an afterthought. The former Detroit Piston, Atlanta Hawk and Washington Wizard missed the 2024-25 season because of a torn ACL before shipping to New Orleans in the Jordan Poole-CJ McCollum swap.

Bey responded to his new circumstances with the best season of his career. He started 64 games (out of 72 total played) last season and averaged a career-high 17.7 points. He made 37% of his 3s and showed improvement as a perimeter defender.

So the Pelicans gave him a big raise, from $6.6 million in this upcoming season to an average of $18.5 million over the following three years, which will keep Bey in New Orleans through his age-30 season. That's a solid contract for a solid player.

It's a bit less clear how New Orleans plans to structure its wing rotation in the short and long term, with Bey, Bennedict Mathurin, Trey Murphy III and Herbert Jones all worthy of playing time, to say nothing of Zion Williamson and/or Derik Queen grabbing minutes at power forward.

To that end, it's possible that Bey's new contract could make New Orleans more amenable to a trade of Murphy or Jones, two more established wings who could fetch draft picks from contenders.

Sept 3: Rockets, Amen Thompson agree to five-year deal

Amen Thompson terms:  Five years, $208 million

Grade: A-

Thompson is the second member of the 2023 draft class to sign a rookie extension this summer, following in the steps of No. 1 pick Victor Wembanyama. That order tracks, as Thompson is the second-best player from that draft class after Wembanyama.

He might not have exploded into superstardom as some expected -- and as Wembanyama did -- last season, but Thompson still fits the profile of a future two-way star. He's only 23 years old, he's one of the NBA's fiercest perimeter defenders and he boosted both his points (18.3 per game) and assists (5.3 per game) last season while leading the NBA in minutes played.

Thompson's 3-point shot remains a glaring hole in his game, as he's at just 22% from distance in his career on low volume. That weakness could limit his ultimate upside, as he might be best suited as an ace defender
